data.narrative:
Tokamak Energy, a Series C nuclear energy company founded by David Kingham, Mikhail Gryaznevich, and Alan Sykes, has raised $335M+ to date. The broader nuclear sector comp universe includes 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private companies, though the narrow peer set at identical stage and valuation tier proved insufficient for statistical median pricing.

Stage-progression analysis is the primary applicable method, using the $335M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C-to-next-stage advancement. This yields a $570M implied valuation. A peer-median approach was not viable; while 5 nuclear-sector peers exist, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier companies produced fewer than 3 datapoints needed for robust comparison. Relying on all-sector medians risked undue distortion given the specialized nature of fusion technology development.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $484M (low) to $655M (median $570M), anchored primarily to stage-based progression. Key uncertainties include the sustainability of nuclear-sector multiples across technology substrates (fusion vs. fission), the dependency of Tokamak Energy's value on near-term technical milestones, and the limited trading history and public liquidity of comparable companies. The range reflects single-method derivation and should be stress-tested against achievement of Series C deployment and financing milestones.
